result:
`bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (7 tests, 3 files) both pass.

I added a public JSON feed at `GET /api/posts`, named `api.posts.index`. `routes/api.ts` is a new registrar (mirroring `routes/auth.ts`, wired in from `registerWebRoutes` in `routes/web.ts`) that registers the route under an `/api` group with no middleware — no session, no CSRF — declaring its contract on the route itself: `query: ApiListPostsQuerySchema` (a new schema in `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts` coercing `page` to a positive int defaulting to 1 and optional `author` to a positive int), plus `resource: { data: [PostResource] }` so the generated client types `json()`, the same way `posts.search` does. Because the query schema is bound to the route, the router validates it before the controller and answers 422 with a JSON `{ message, errors }` body for `?page=0`, `?page=abc`, `?author=abc`, `?author=0`; `guren codegen` was re-run, so `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` and `.guren/routes.gen.ts` now carry `'api.posts.index': { method: 'GET', path: '/api/posts', response: { data: Array<Data.Post> } }`. `PostController.apiIndex` (in the existing controller, alongside the other post actions) serves it: newest-first, 10 per page, optionally filtered by `authorId`, returning `{ data, meta, links }` with each post rendered through `PostResource` (so `id`, `title`, `excerpt`, `body`, `createdAt` ISO string and the `author` object). It slices the page by hand with `count()` + `limit/offset/get()` rather than the ORM's `paginate({ page, perPage })` for two reasons found while testing: that path returns rows without resolving `with('author')` (the author would have been missing from every item), and it clamps an out-of-range page back onto the last one, which would make a consumer walking pages until `data` is empty loop forever — now a page past the end returns empty `data` with the requested `currentPage`. New tests in `tests/ApiPostController.test.ts` cover the route's presence in the manifest and the four 422 cases; like the existing starter tests they need no migrations or fixtures, and I separately verified the listing, filtering, and 27-post pagination behaviour against the local test database with a temporary probe.
